-          member token. Session exports HTTP middleware, a public sessionService, initSession,
-          getOriginOfRequest, a per-call createSessionFromToken factory and deleteAllSessions bound
-          to its private store. Session-service operations close over collaborators rather than
-          requiring a receiver. Workflow functions return promises, while setup assertion creation
-          and SSO middleware creation are synchronous. API-key units check successful request key
-          identity and selected error codes using fake model lookups; the member-token unit checks
-          the function and negative/fallthrough paths with a fake public configuration, not the
-          whole root shape, binding identity or a successful real member-token request.
-          Source shows several independent lifetimes. Loading session constructs a GhostMailer,
-          closure-based session service and HTTP middleware, and imports the eagerly constructed
-          SessionStore that retains models.Session. Express middleware is created and cached on
-          the first getSession call without an existing req.session; it captures the session
-          secret and cookie options then. Each member-token getter returns a new wrapper, sharing
-          middleware cached only after awaited creation, so concurrent first calls can construct
-          multiple instances. Each SSO factory call retrieves the shared adapter, replaces its
-          user repository and binds its methods into new middleware. The root provides no reset
-          of these private instances. Factory units inject collaborators; no cited test asserts
-          real root import, first-use identity, overlapping creation or construction failure.
-          Admin and Content router middleware retain auth arrays/functions when their modules
-          load. The backend constructs SSO middleware for /ghost; session, authentication and
-          users endpoints retain the root and access its session/workflow getters during work.
-          Authentication also retains a scheduling adapter and Users instance for reset; Users
-          receives auth as a currently unused collaborator. These bindings are source-checked.
-          Real HTTP tests assert login/logout access, emailed-code verification, cross-origin
-          refusal, fresh-session code refusal, password-change/reset invalidation of other and
-          cloned sessions, and successful reset of a locked account from an intercepted email.
-          SSO HTTP uses a substituted adapter with real user/session composition and asserts
-          active-owner access and inactive/missing-credential refusal. These tests do not prove
-          external SSO identity validation or preservation of retained callers across replacement.
